analyst_view.overall: Early view: Promoted Schalke are 17th and have not scored in a home league game this season, and Miron Muslić is waiting on news of goalkeeper Loris Karius and Robin Gosens after both were hurt in a collision at Hoffenheim. Stuttgart arrive on two straight league wins but with Angelo Stiller among several injured regulars and a Champions League match in the following week.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean lower: all five of Schalke's league goals have come away from home, and their games have produced only 16 goals in nine, the fewest in the league. Stuttgart scored just once against Bremen in their last outing.

corners.text: The site expects 10.5 corners, 6.1 for Stuttgart. Stuttgart's wing-backs push high in their 3-4-2-1 and Schalke will defend deep, which supports the number, but Schalke's home attack creates little pressure of its own. I stay close to it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. I lean slightly higher: a Schalke side fighting relegation in front of a full Veltins Arena will be aggressive, and Stuttgart's game at Leverkusen produced seven yellow cards in an hour. Schalke themselves took two bookings in each of their last two games.

shots.text: The site has 27.9 shots, 12.7 for Schalke. Schalke did create a lot at Hoffenheim (expected goals above 2.5), but at home they have been blunt, and Stuttgart may manage the game with Champions League football days later. I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. With Schalke yet to score at home and possibly without Gosens, whom one injury tracker lists out until mid-December with a knee problem, I expect fewer on-target efforts from the hosts. Stuttgart's Ermedin Demirović and Deniz Undav should provide most of the total.
